item.title: Getting started with Speedle Cloud
item.description: Speedle Cloud is in public beta. This guide describes the workflow for the live service. Sign in with GitHub or Google Open the Cloud console in your browser and sign in with an available provider. For a new identity with an unused verified email address, confirm Create account. If the email is already in use, sign in with the linked provider shown by the console. Create a service and a policy Open the Service workspace, enter books, and choose Create service.

item.title: Speedle Cloud Console user manual
item.description: Speedle Cloud is in public beta. The free public beta is for evaluation and learning, has no SLA and is not recommended for production use. Features and limits may change. This manual walks through everyday tasks in the Speedle Cloud Console (SCC) at cloud.speedle.io. For a quick end-to-end API call from your server, see Getting started. For endpoint payloads, error codes and quotas, see the Authorization API, API reference and Limits and errors.

item.title: Speedle Cloud API keys
item.description: API keys belong to a workspace and can access its services according to their scope. They authenticate your application, not its end users. Managing API keys, sessions and linked identities always requires a signed-in console session. Removing a workspace member or leaving a workspace does not revoke API keys that person created; review and revoke them explicitly when needed. Speedle Cloud is in public beta. This guide describes the workflow for the live service.

item.title: Global roles
item.description: Speedle Cloud is in public beta. This guide describes the workflow for the live service. A role assignment usually belongs to one service. When several services in the same workspace share the same assignment, define it once in the workspace’s Global roles service and use the role in each service’s own authorization policies. Only role policies are supported there. A global role assignment does not grant any operation by itself: every service still defines the permissions it allows.

item.title: Speedle Cloud authorization API
item.description: Speedle Cloud is in public beta. This guide describes the workflow for the live service. Use a workspace API key for server-side authorization calls. Sign in to your account, select the target workspace and create keys there. Use ads or pms:read+ads for ADS checks; pms:read and pms:write return 403 insufficient_scope. The combined pms:read+ads scope also permits PMS reads and is required for policy synchronization with Speedle Cloud ADS (speedle-cloud); it cannot write policies.

item.title: Speedle Cloud Limits and errors
item.description: Speedle Cloud is in public beta. This guide describes the workflow for the live service. Limits apply to the whole workspace unless a row says otherwise. API keys are workspace credentials; changing keys in the same workspace does not increase the daily quota.
